sentences.text: This animal belongs to the group Crocodylomorpha, which includes ancestors of modern crocodiles. It is a sphenosuchian, a basal relative of today's crocodilians.
It was a tiny creature with a skull measuring 164 mm and a total body length of 1.3 meters. Its body was slender, featuring long limbs, a long tail, and a pointed snout.
The upper jaws possessed a unique hole designed to let an enlarged lower tooth pass through.
Unlike modern crocodiles, this species lived on land rather than in water.
The genus was named in 1965 by D.J. Simmons using fossils found by Father Oehler near Huangchiatien.
More remains were later recovered in 1985 by a joint Chinese-US expedition.
Scientists originally thought it was an ornithosuchid thecodont before reclassifying it as a sphenosuchian.
Fossils come from Lower Jurassic rocks in Yunnan, China, dating to about 186 million years ago. The animal lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
A second species, D. xingsuensis, was named by Wu in 1986 but is now considered a synonym of D. elaphros.
